# SLURM Command Reference {#sec-appendix-slurm}

This appendix is a compact reference for SLURM (Simple Linux Utility for Resource Management) [@yoo2003slurm] commands and directives on clusters like Talapas. The concepts behind them (fair-share scheduling, right-sizing, pipeline design) are explained in @sec-hpc-talapas.

## The Ten Commands You Will Actually Use {#sec-common-commands-ref}

| Task | Command |
|:-----|:--------|
| Submit a batch script | `sbatch script.sh` |
| Submit with a one-off override | `sbatch --mem=64G --time=08:00:00 script.sh` |
| Interactive shell on a compute node | `srun --account=myPIRG --partition=interactive --time=2:00:00 --cpus-per-task=2 --mem=8G --pty bash` |
| List your jobs (with pending reason) | `squeue -u $USER` |
| Estimated start time of a pending job | `squeue -j JOBID --start` |
| Cancel a job / all your pending jobs | `scancel JOBID` / `scancel -u $USER -t PENDING` |
| Efficiency report for a finished job | `seff JOBID` |
| Accounting fields for a finished job | `sacct -j JOBID --format=JobID,ReqMem,MaxRSS,Elapsed,State,ExitCode` |
| Everything SLURM knows about a job | `scontrol show job JOBID` |
| Partition and node availability | `sinfo` |

: The SLURM commands used day to day {#tbl-common-commands-ref}

### Reading `seff` and Right-Sizing {#sec-rightsizing-ref}

Run `seff JOBID` after every job. The loop: first run with a modest over-estimate; then set the next run from what was actually used.

| `seff` line | Use it to set |
|:------------|:--------------|
| `State: COMPLETED` (else `FAILED`, `OUT_OF_MEMORY`, `TIMEOUT`, `CANCELLED`) | Whether to trust the output at all; read the `.err` log if not `COMPLETED` |
| `Memory Utilized` (= `MaxRSS` in `sacct`) | Next `--mem` = this × 1.2 |
| `Memory Efficiency` | Under 50%? Shrink `--mem` |
| `Job Wall-clock time` (= `Elapsed`) | Next `--time` = this × 1.2 |
| `CPU Efficiency` | Low on a multi-core request means the tool is not using the cores; reduce `--cpus-per-task` |

: Turning `seff` output into the next job's requests {#tbl-seff-ref}

Defaults on Talapas if you do not specify: about 3.7 GB memory per core, 1 core, and the partition's maximum time (24 h on `compute`). There is no default partition or account; both are required.

### Why Is My Job Pending? {#sec-pd-reasons-ref}

Shown in the `NODELIST(REASON)` column of `squeue -u $USER`.

| Reason | Meaning | Action |
|:-------|:--------|:-------|
| `Priority` | Higher fair-share priority jobs are ahead | Wait |
| `Resources` | Requested resources not free yet | Wait; check requests are not oversized |
| `QOSMaxCpuPerUserLimit` / `QOSMaxJobsPerUserLimit` / `QOSMaxMemoryPerUser` | Per-user cap on cores / jobs / memory reached | Wait for your own jobs to finish; throttle arrays with `%M` |
| `ReqNodeNotAvail, Reserved for maintenance` | `--time` runs into a maintenance window | Shorten `--time` or add `--time-min` |
| `PartitionTimeLimit` | `--time` exceeds the partition maximum | Shorten, or use the `*long` partition |
| `AssocGrpCPUMinutesLimit` | PIRG allocation exhausted | Contact RACS |
| `Dependency` | Waiting on `--dependency=` job | Normal |
| `InvalidAccount` | `--account` missing or wrong | `groups`; fix `--account=` |

: Common pending reasons {#tbl-pd-reasons-ref}

## SBATCH Directives {#sec-sbatch-directives}

### Essential Directives {#sec-essential-directives}

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=my_job       # Job name (displayed in queue)
#SBATCH --partition=compute     # Partition to use (required)
#SBATCH --account=PIRG          # Account to charge (required)
#SBATCH --time=04:00:00         # Time limit (HH:MM:SS or D-HH:MM:SS)
#SBATCH --nodes=1               # Number of nodes
#SBATCH --ntasks=1              # Number of tasks (MPI ranks)
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4       # CPUs per task (threads)
#SBATCH --mem=16G               # Memory per node

set -euo pipefail               # stop on error / unset var / failed pipe stage
module purge                    # modules must be loaded INSIDE the script
module load R/4.3.3
```

### Output Directives {#sec-output-directives}

```bash
#SBATCH --output=output_%j.log  # Standard output (%j = job ID)
#SBATCH --error=error_%j.log    # Standard error
#SBATCH --output=%x_%j.out      # %x = job name
#SBATCH --mail-user=email@uoregon.edu  # Email address
#SBATCH --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL     # When to email
```

### Resource Directives {#sec-resource-directives}

```bash
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=4G        # Memory per CPU
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1            # Request 1 GPU
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:v100:2       # Request 2 V100 GPUs
#SBATCH --constraint=intel      # Node constraint
#SBATCH --exclusive             # Exclusive node access
#SBATCH --array=1-100           # Job array
#SBATCH --array=1-100%10        # Array with max 10 running
```

### Dependency Directives {#sec-dependency-directives}

```bash
#SBATCH --dependency=afterok:JOBID      # Run after job succeeds
#SBATCH --dependency=afterany:JOBID     # Run after job completes
#SBATCH --dependency=afternotok:JOBID   # Run after job fails
#SBATCH --dependency=singleton          # Only one job with this name
```

## Complete SBATCH Directive Reference {#sec-sbatch-reference}

| Directive | Description | Example |
|:----------|:------------|:--------|
| `--job-name` / `-J` | Job name | `--job-name=analysis` |
| `--partition` / `-p` | Partition | `--partition=compute` |
| `--account` / `-A` | Account | `--account=myPIRG` |
| `--time` / `-t` | Time limit; exceeded → `TIMEOUT` | `--time=04:00:00` |
| `--time-min` | Minimum acceptable time (lets backfill start the job in a shorter gap) | `--time-min=01:00:00` |
| `--nodes` / `-N` | Number of nodes | `--nodes=2` |
| `--ntasks` / `-n` | Number of tasks | `--ntasks=8` |
| `--ntasks-per-node` | Tasks per node | `--ntasks-per-node=4` |
| `--cpus-per-task` / `-c` | CPUs per task | `--cpus-per-task=4` |
| `--mem` | Memory per node; exceeded → `OUT_OF_MEMORY` | `--mem=32G` |
| `--mem-per-cpu` | Memory per CPU | `--mem-per-cpu=4G` |
| `--gres` | Generic resources | `--gres=gpu:1` |
| `--output` / `-o` | Stdout file (`%j` job ID, `%x` name, `%A_%a` array) | `--output=logs/%x_%j.out` |
| `--error` / `-e` | Stderr file (omit to merge into `--output`) | `--error=logs/%x_%j.err` |
| `--mail-user` | Email address | `--mail-user=me@uoregon.edu` |
| `--mail-type` | Email events | `--mail-type=ALL` |
| `--array` | Job array (`%M` = max concurrent) | `--array=1-100%10` |
| `--dependency` | Job dependencies | `--dependency=afterok:123` |
| `--constraint` | Node features | `--constraint=intel` |
| `--exclusive` | Exclusive access | `--exclusive` |
| `--nodelist` | Specific nodes | `--nodelist=n[001-004]` |
| `--exclude` | Exclude nodes | `--exclude=n001` |
| `--qos` | Quality of service | `--qos=long` |
| `--reservation` | Use reservation | `--reservation=workshop` |

## Job Arrays {#sec-job-arrays}

### Template: One Script, Many Samples {#sec-array-template-ref}

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=align
#SBATCH --partition=compute
#SBATCH --account=myPIRG
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --array=1-24%8               # 24 tasks, at most 8 running at once
#SBATCH --output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out   # %A = array job ID, %a = task ID
#SBATCH --error=logs/%x_%A_%a.err

set -euo pipefail
module purge
module load bwa/0.7.17 samtools/1.17

SAMPLE=$(sed -n "${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}p" samples.txt)   # line N = task N
OUT="results/${SAMPLE}.bam"
[[ -s "$OUT" ]] && { echo "$SAMPLE done, skipping"; exit 0; }   # resumable

bwa mem -t "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" ref.fa "raw/${SAMPLE}_R1.fastq.gz" "raw/${SAMPLE}_R2.fastq.gz" \
    | samtools sort -@ "$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" -o "$OUT.tmp"
mv "$OUT.tmp" "$OUT"          # rename only after success: no truncated outputs
echo "Wrote $OUT"
```

Run `mkdir -p logs results` before submitting. The `logs/` directory must exist or the job fails silently.

### Array Index Variants {#sec-array-variants-ref}

```bash
#SBATCH --array=0-100:10        # 0, 10, 20, ..., 100
#SBATCH --array=1-1000%50       # Max 50 running at once
#SBATCH --array=3,7,12          # Rerun only specific tasks
```

To size the array from a file at submit time: `sbatch --array=1-$(wc -l < samples.txt) align.sh`. To run a step only after every task succeeds: `sbatch --dependency=afterok:ARRAY_JOB_ID next_step.sh`.

## Example Job Scripts {#sec-example-scripts}

### Basic R Script {#sec-example-r}

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=r_analysis
#SBATCH --partition=compute
#SBATCH --account=myPIRG
#SBATCH --time=02:00:00
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=16G
#SBATCH --output=r_job_%j.log

# Load required modules
module load R/4.3.3

# Run R script
Rscript my_analysis.R
```

### Python with Conda {#sec-example-python}

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=python_job
#SBATCH --partition=compute
#SBATCH --account=myPIRG
#SBATCH --time=04:00:00
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --output=python_%j.log

# Load conda and activate your environment
module load miniconda3/20240410
conda activate myenv

# Run Python script
python analysis.py --input data.csv --output results/
```

### GPU Job {#sec-example-gpu}

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=gpu_job
#SBATCH --partition=gpu
#SBATCH --account=myPIRG
#SBATCH --time=08:00:00
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=4
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --output=gpu_%j.log

module load cuda/12.4
module load miniconda3/20240410
conda activate ml_env

python train_model.py
```

### MPI Job {#sec-example-mpi}

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=mpi_job
#SBATCH --partition=compute
#SBATCH --account=myPIRG
#SBATCH --time=04:00:00
#SBATCH --nodes=4
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=16
#SBATCH --mem-per-cpu=4G
#SBATCH --output=mpi_%j.log

module load openmpi/4.1

mpirun -np 64 ./my_mpi_program
```

## Talapas-Specific Information {#sec-talapas-specific}

### Common Partitions {#sec-talapas-partitions}

| Partition | Description | Time Limit |
|:----------|:------------|:-----------|
| `compute` | Standard CPU nodes | 1 day |
| `computelong` | Extended-time CPU jobs | 14 days |
| `gpu` | GPU nodes | 1 day |
| `gpulong` | Extended-time GPU jobs | 14 days |
| `interactive` | Interactive CPU sessions | 12 hours |
| `interactivegpu` | Interactive GPU sessions | 8 hours |
| `memory` | High-memory nodes (up to 4 TB) | 1 day |
| `memorylong` | Extended-time high-memory jobs | 14 days |

: Talapas partitions {#tbl-talapas-partitions}

Run `sinfo` to list every partition, including your lab's condo partitions. Interactive sessions should use `--partition=interactive` (or `interactivegpu`).

### Storage Locations {#sec-talapas-storage-ref}

| Location | Quota | Purpose |
|:---------|:------|:--------|
| `/home/$USER` | 250 GB | Config files, small data |
| `/projects/PIRG/$USER` | Shared (2 TB default) | Large data, analysis |
| `/projects/PIRG/shared` | Shared | Shared group data |
| `/scratch/PIRG` | Large per-PIRG quota | Working data; **purged after 90 days without access** |
| `$SLURM_TMPDIR` | Local | Temporary scratch |

: Talapas storage. Nothing is backed up by RACS; use Globus for large transfers (@sec-file-transfer). {#tbl-talapas-storage}
